passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: The enacted text makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student, and sends the per-student monies to a "nongovernmental primary or secondary school" of the parent's choosing.
Payne is listed as a co-sponsor of the bill, which the Governor signed as Chapter 388.

rows.reasoning: Payne co-sponsored and voted Y on final passage of HB2853 (2022), a single-subject bill whose added section 15-2401.01 makes any resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" a qualified student for an empowerment scholarship account, and whose section 15-2402 transfers the monies that would otherwise go to the student's school district into that account for tuition "at a qualified school", defined as "a nongovernmental primary or secondary school" with no exclusion of religious schools. That is universal eligibility with the money following the student to a school the family picks, which matches "Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family" rather than the "most families" or income-capped rungs. The 2022 acts are from his service in the Arizona House, the other chamber of this legislature, so they count for this seat.
